descriptionChirho: The noun kohen (כָּהֵן) meaning 'priest' — a cultic/religious functionary, appearing here in both plural determined forms (the priests, and the priests, his priests) and singular determined form (the priest). English renders as priest/priests; Spanish sacerdote(s); Hindi याजक (yaajak) / याजकों (yajakon, plural); Arabic الكاهِن (al-kahin, sg.) / الكَهَنَة (al-kahana, pl.); Korean 제사장 (jesajang) / 제사장들 (jesajangdeul, plural); Swahili kuhani (sg.) / makuhani (pl.). The difference between the two clusters is purely number inflection (singular vs. plural), which is a grammatical distinction, not a semantic one. All 8 occurrences denote the same role of priestly office.
